expectations.evidence: operationState.phase: Succeeded with message 'successfully synced (all tasks run)'; reasons from it that this is not a sync failure.

expectations.text: Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy

expectations.text: Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
expectations.evidence: Inspects live Deployment image, Deployment conditions (Available=True, Progressing=False ProgressDeadlineExceeded), both ReplicaSets with per-RS image and readyReplicas, and the failing pod via namespace events.

expectations.evidence: Events show 'Failed to pull image registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/nonexistent-eval:9.9.9 ... Repo not found' and ImagePullBackOff.

No unsupported link in the chain.

expectations.text: Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
expectations.evidence: currentStepIndex: 6 against a 6-step list; explains 0-based status index vs 1-based CLI display and maps 'step 2' to either pause{duration:30s} (index 1) or setWeight 50 (index 2).

expectations.text: Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
expectations.evidence: Shows RolloutPaused=False in status.conditions and distinguishes an indefinite `pause: {}` (manual, blocks forever) from a timed pause and from analysis-driven blocking.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved
expectations.evidence: Lists all three AnalysisRuns and inspects canary-demo-6c8df69c96-2-3, including its labels (step-index 3 = the analysis step) and status.

expectations.evidence: No direct CRD query is run; argoproj.io CRD existence appears only incidentally inside the CSV requirementStatus output (applications/applicationsets/argocds/rollouts .argoproj.io listed as installed alongside v1.21.3).

expectations.evidence: `oc get pods -n openshift-gitops` shown with ages/restarts, plus the operator-namespace pod listing with restart counts.

expectations.text: Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
expectations.evidence: ArgoCD CR custom-columns show SERVER/REPO/CTRL/REDIS/SSO per instance, and the pod listing confirms application-controller, repo-server and server pods.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: Full ApplicationSet yaml including spec.strategy.type RollingSync and both rollingSync.steps matchExpressions.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Steps shown as envLabel In [staging] then In [production]; explicitly states production is step 2, and verifies the generated Application carries envLabel=staging so the selectors do match.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: The health gate is checked with live output (staging Progressing/ImagePullBackOff, so step 1 can never complete), but maxUpdate is never mentioned even to note that it is unset.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: eval-staging per-resource health shown, deployment image does-not-exist-eval, pod in ImagePullBackOff, and the Application's Progressing health.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: Explicit: RollingSync advances only when every Application in the preceding step is both Synced and Healthy; one permanently-Progressing app blocks later steps with no timeout and no abort.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Root cause (progressive syncs not enabled, so spec.strategy is inert) is backed by the absent status.applicationStatus, empty controller args/env, the ArgoCD CR spec.applicationSet, argocd-cmd-params-cm, and a controller log showing both Applications created in one reconcile; production is shown Synced/Healthy, which the answer uses to contradict the premise rather than ignore it.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: Shows checkout-api and namespace prod do not exist, then retrieves both real blue-green Rollouts with spec.strategy.blueGreen printed in full.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: Explains autoPromotionEnabled defaults to true, that an explicit false is an opt-in manual gate, and that an hour at preview with no promotion is configured behaviour rather than a fault.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: Explains prePromotionAnalysis and postPromotionAnalysis and states neither real rollout configures prePromotionAnalysis, backed by `oc get analysisruns -A` listing only canary-demo runs.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: activeService/previewService shown for both rollouts; activeSelector == previewSelector is used to establish that bluegreen-demo cut over, and the finance rollout's service pair is shown.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: Explains blue-green promotion mechanics but never makes the required contrast explicit - that blue-green has no steps[]/currentStepIndex and therefore no step-based automatic progression.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: The central premise correction is right and anchored in the configuration shown, but a load-bearing mechanism claim - that prePromotionAnalysis is gated by auto-promotion and only starts once you promote - is asserted with no supporting output and is not how blue-green pre-promotion analysis behaves.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocds.argoproj.io -A` with per-instance status columns detects three instances across three namespaces.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: All three listed by namespace/name with role, route and Application count in a table.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Investigates all three and gives each its own clearly separated subsection of findings.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Ambiguity is disclosed up front; no silent selection - the final answer names which instance to look at only after reporting all three.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Per-instance structure: team-b-gitops/team-b (clean, zero restarts, no controller errors), openshift-gitops-operator/argocd (idle, argocd-server OOMKilled 11x), openshift-gitops/openshift-gitops (all problem Applications, argo-rollouts 635 restarts), plus a separately labelled operator-level finding shared by all three.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Application yaml retrieved; status.health.status Suspended with lastTransitionTime, alongside sync Synced and operationState Succeeded.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: States plainly that Suspended is not an error state - it is what Argo CD assigns to an intentionally halted resource (paused Rollout, suspended CronJob, suspended workflow) and is distinct from Degraded and Progressing.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
expectations.evidence: Inspects the Rollout and cites spec.paused: true, status.phase Paused and health message 'manually paused'; also uses managedFields to show kubectl-patch set it 10s after argocd-controller created the object.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: Explicitly says nothing is broken about the suspension and frames resumption as the decision the pause was waiting for, while warning that unpausing exposes a second, separate defect.

expectations.text: Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Separates the two clearly: a section headed 'One thing that is worth a look (but is not the Suspended cause)' and an explicit statement that the probe/image defect does not cause the Suspended health.

expectations.text: Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Pod phase and restart count are shown (0/1 Running, 8 restarts, lastState exitCode 0 Completed) and probe-failure events are quoted, but no Service endpoints check is made, and the stated reason the workload is not Available - that the httpd-24 s2i image's default entrypoint exits rather than serving, so nothing ever listens on port 80 - is backed by no container log and is contradicted by this same answer's event output 'Container helm-guestbook failed liveness probe, will be restarted', i.e. kubelet is terminating it rather than it exiting on its own.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Shows spec.sources with two entries and treats the Application as multi-source throughout, including the 'source 1 of 2' semantics.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Both entries are shown and discussed individually: source 1 repoURL/path helm-guestbook/targetRevision HEAD/helm.valueFiles $values/envs/production/values.yaml; source 2 repoURL/targetRevision HEAD/ref values, and notes both repoURLs are identical.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the ref: values source (source 2) as the failing one - the $values checkout does not contain envs/production/values.yaml - and explains why the error text names source 1.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Never collapses to single-source: the whole analysis is about which of the two sources owns the missing file, plus generic multi-source isolation guidance.

expectations.text: Produces a report naming WHICH source is failing — by its index or repoURL/chart, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must be consistent with the evidence shown: if the error names one source, the report must not attribute the failure to the other.
expectations.evidence: Names the source by index and repoURL and gives a concrete fix (repoint /spec/sources/1/repoURL, or drop the indirection), and explains the discrepancy with the error text. Against the literal consistency clause, though, the shown error names 'source 1 of 2' while the report attributes the failure to source 2 - an expectation I found ambiguous, applied identically to both files.
